newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Bosnian Serb Hardliners ask Plavsic to yield power.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb Hardliners ask Plavsic to yield power.

text.p: Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic has been expelled by hardline nationalist opponents from the ruling SDS party and asked to turn over power to her vice-president, the Bosnian Serb news agency SRNA said on Sunday.
The decision to remove Plavsic was unanimous following her her threat to arrest former president and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic for corruption, the report added.
Hardliners have accused Plavsic of being too cooperative with international mediators who also want to arrest Karadzic and other accused Bosnian Serbs for trial by the U.N. war crimes tribunal.
Their fears have hardened since British troops captured a war crimes suspect in the northern town of Prijedor this month and shot dead another who resisted arrest.

NATO forces and international observers have been the target of a series of minor retaliatory explosions, the latest of which occurred in Plavsic's Banja Luka stronghold last night. No injuries were reported in the two blasts.

The decision to expel Plavsic from the party brings the conflict to a head after earlier attempts by nationalist leaders to seek a compromise over her attempts to dissolve parliament and call fresh elections.
